title: Open-closed short exact sequence on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ the inclusion of the complementary open subscheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and assume that $j$ is quasi-compact. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $i^*,j^*$ be the inverse images and $i_*$ the direct image of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and $j_!$ the extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Then for every sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the sequence
$$
0\longrightarrow j_!j^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal F\longrightarrow i_*i^*\mathcal F\longrightarrow0,
$$
whose first map is the counit of $j_!\dashv j^*$ and whose second map is the unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$, is exact.

source.place: Pro-etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 09AH (label lemma-ses-associated-to-open); also literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Lemma 6.1.9 (surjectivity of $F\to i_*i^*F$) and Lemma 6.1.11 ($j_!j^*F=\ker(F\to i_*i^*F)$), p. 43, for $X$ qcqs and $U$ qcqs

proof.text: Put $A=\Lambda_X$, the constant sheaf of rings. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] to $i$ and $j$: its commutative-coefficient clause says that the particular structure maps $c^i_\Lambda:i^{-1}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_Z$ and $c^j_\Lambda:j^{-1}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] are isomorphisms, preserving constant sections. Thus coefficients in the ringed sequence can be identified with the specified constant coefficients, using these maps rather than an arbitrary ring isomorphism. No qcqs assumption on $X$, constructibility of $\mathcal F$, or geometric-stalk detection is involved. In the current definition, $c^f_\Lambda=\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_{\mathrm{dom}(f)}}\circ f^{-1}(\rho^f_\Lambda)$, with $\rho^f_\Lambda$ the sheaf map extending constant sections; this is precisely the adjoint map named by the comparison theorem.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with the ring sheaf $A=\Lambda_X$ and the $A$-module $M=\mathcal F$. Its short-exact-sequence clause gives $0\to j_!j^{-1}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\to i_*i^{-1}\mathcal F\to0$ with the counit and unit maps, where the coefficients on $U,Z$ are $j^{-1}A,i^{-1}A$. Its hypotheses are exactly the closed immersion, its complementary open immersion, and quasi-compactness of $j$ already assumed here. The extra qcqs hypothesis in its last sentence belongs only to its filtered-colimit assertion, which is not used.

proof.text: Identify the functors and the actual arrows. For $f=i,j$, write $c=c^f_\Lambda$. Under step 1 the module pullback of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] has the canonical isomorphism $f^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{f^{-1}\Lambda_X}\Lambda_{\mathrm{dom}(f)}\to f^{-1}\mathcal F$, $m\otimes b\mapsto c^{-1}(b)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. These formulas commute with restrictions and hence define inverse sheaf maps. Direct image is the same sectionwise sheaf, with scalar action through $\rho^f_{\Lambda,V}:\Lambda_X(V)\to\Lambda_{\mathrm{dom}(f)}(u_f(V))$ as specified in the current definition, so this identification also identifies $i_*i^*\mathcal F$ with the last term of step 2. The definition [def-weil-extension-by-zero] sheafifies exactly the extension-by-zero presheaf specified in the ringed node: the value is the restricted module on an object factoring through $U$, and zero otherwise. Thus the first term is $j_!j^*\mathcal F$. The counit on this presheaf sends the section over an object factoring through $U$ to that same section of $\mathcal F$; it is zero on the other presheaf values. Write $q_f:f^{-1}\mathcal F\to f^*\mathcal F$ for $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ and $\theta_f:f^*\mathcal F\to f^{-1}\mathcal F$ for the displayed inverse. The module adjunction unit is $f_*(q_f)\circ\eta_{f,\mathcal F}$, so $f_*(\theta_f)$ carries it to $\eta_{f,\mathcal F}$ because $\theta_f q_f=\mathrm{id}$. The module adjunction counit on a sheaf $G$ is given locally by $m\otimes b\mapsto b\,\varepsilon_{f,G}(m)$; after $\theta_f$ it is the underlying counit. The scalar compatibility follows from $c^f_\Lambda=\varepsilon_f\circ f^{-1}(\rho^f_\Lambda)$, so these formulas use the specified structure maps. For $j$, the restriction identification over $U$ makes the extension-by-zero counit the section map just described. Consequently the two term identifications carry the arrows of step 2 to precisely the counit and unit in the statement. Since the middle identification is the identity and the outer identifications are invertible, monomorphisms, epimorphisms, and image-equals-kernel are preserved: composing with these inverses identifies the kernels and images as subobjects. Epimorphism here is in the sheaf category; no sectionwise surjectivity is asserted. This is the required short exact sequence.
